episode.title: Corrections, Trust, and the Long Game
episode.description: A. correspondent talks with Renee Montagne-Park: Corrections, Trust, and the Long Game.

bullets: A correction is a reliability signal, not a failure, because it reveals the system's ability to self-correct and maintain integrity over time.
Managing the risk of being wrong in public is its own discipline — the framing of error determines the trade-offs teams make.
Ignoring the signal of a correction leads to rebuilding systems from scratch, as seen in teams using NPR and BBC.
Reliability is not about avoiding errors but about how systems respond to them — the response defines resilience.
The most underrated piece of reliability is the act of correcting publicly, which validates the system's trustworthiness.
Risk management is not a standalone function but a cross-cutting discipline that shapes all other decisions.
Running an idea for two weeks to test its viability enables iteration without overcommitting to a single path.
The discipline of public correction enables teams to maintain long-term reliability rather than short-term fixes.
